subject: POC kickoff & hands-on session — availability and run-handoff
messages:
From: Jill Parker <jill.parker@acme.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: devops@acme.io
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC planning — aligning on hands-on + load run

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We'd like to lock in a hands-on POC kickoff where your team can run the load/benchmark and walk our engineers through the prompt routing and caching behavior. High level asks: 
- Two-hour hands-on session (dry run + full load run)
- Verify throughput to 120–150 req/s for our typical batched traffic
- Validate 95th pct latency keeps under 200ms for small prompts, and an end-to-end SLA implication for larger prompts (~1k tokens)

Our primary attendees: me (Jill Parker), Raj Singh (platform), and two SREs (devops@acme.io).

Availability window: May 5–7 (PST). Do you have a preferred slot? Also please share the runbook and any preflight checklist (credentials, test harness, sample prompts).

Thanks,
Jill
Jill Parker
Director of AI Platform — Acme Corp
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jill Parker <jill.parker@acme.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC planning — aligning on hands-on + load run

Jill — thanks for the clear asks. We're excited to run this. Proposed plan: 
1) Quick 30-min preflight (credentials, access, region) the day before.
2) 2-hour hands-on session: 30m prompt & routing review, 30m test harness walkthrough + dry run, 60m full throughput run.

Slots we have open (PST): May 5, 10:00–12:00; May 6, 13:00–15:00; May 7, 08:00–10:00. Please confirm which works best for your team.

Preflight checklist (attached runbook): service account + temp API key, sample prompts, load harness config (we'll provide a container image + traffic generator), and a small dataset for prompt quality checks. 

Marissa will lead the load/benchmark portion; Soojin will own infra & region pinning. We'll share the runbook and the harness config by EOD.

If you want a dry run (recommended) we can schedule a 30-min slot the morning of the main session.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Quick notes on the benchmark plan from our side: 
- Target throughput: nominal 120 req/s, burst up to 180 req/s to validate autoscaling triggers.
- Latency SLOs we should validate: P50 < 60ms, P95 < 200ms for prompt sizes < 256 tokens. For ~1k token prompts we're expecting higher variance — we'll capture tail latency and token-rate.
- Test harness: we'll use the Redwood client load generator (container). Config attached (load-harness-config.yaml). It supports ramp, hold, and stepped scenarios.

Please send 10–15 representative prompt examples and a short list of user routing rules you care about (e.g., pin user -> model-X, routing by latency vs cost). We'll run two routing scenarios during the session.

Logistics: I recommend May 6, 13:00–15:00 PST (gives time for a May 5 preflight). I'll create the calendar invite once Jill confirms.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
